related_questions.question: Can you get sick from a CO2 leak?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can get sick from a carbon monoxide (CO) leak, and it can be very dangerous. CO is a poisonous gas produced by the incomplete burning of fuels like gas, wood, or coal. It's odorless and colorless, making it difficult to detect without a detector.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, you can get sick from a carbon monoxide (CO) leak

list.snippet: CO replaces oxygen in the bloodstream, depriving the body's organs and tissues of the oxygen they need.
This can lead to a range of symptoms, from mild to severe, depending on the concentration of CO and the duration of exposure.
Mild to moderate: Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, confusion, and chest pain.
Severe: Loss of consciousness, seizures, and even death.

text_blocks.snippet: If you suspect a CO leak:

list.title: 1. Get fresh air immediately:
list.snippet: Open doors and windows, turn off fuel-burning appliances, and leave the area.

list.title: 2. Seek medical attention:
list.snippet: Go to the emergency room and inform the medical staff about the possibility of CO poisoning.

list.title: 3. Get a CO detector:
list.snippet: Install a battery-powered CO detector and replace the batteries regularly, according to the CDC.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: CO poisoning can be fatal, especially for those sleeping or under the influence of alcohol or drugs, as they may not be able to recognize the symptoms in time.
